title: Sin Has a Thousand Treacherous Arts
description: Sin Has a Thousand Treacherous Arts in Tonic Solfa to YORK, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for his Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707), Book II, composed on divine subjects, hymn 150, headed “The deceitfulness of sin”.
Watts' hymns were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Common Metre (8.6.8.6). This page sets the words to YORK; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Sin has a thou-sand treach-erous arts To prac-tise on the mind; With flat-tering looks she tempts our hearts But leaves a sting be-hind.

lines: Sin has a thousand treacherous arts
With flattering looks she tempts our hearts
With names of virtue she deceives
And while the heedless wretch believes,
She pleads for all the joys she brings,
But cheats the soul of heavenly things,
And chains it down to sense.
So on a tree divinely fair
Our mother took the poison there,

source: Isaac Watts, Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to YORK by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
